cases.description: On a pipe whose reader stays open, PipeWriter.CloseWithError(first) followed by CloseWithError(second) returns nil both times without replacing first; a subsequent read receives first.
With one reader and no other operations, after a six-byte Pipe write has delivered two bytes, the reader closes with an error; the writer returns the two consumed bytes together with that error.
On a pipe kept open, a zero-length write still participates in a reader handshake; after a matching zero-length Read both calls return zero and nil.

With strings.NewReader("x") and no prior non-EOF reader error, a split function returning ErrFinalToken with a non-nil empty token makes Scan return true once, then false with nil Err; with a nil token the first Scan is false with nil Err.
Calling Scanner.Buffer or Scanner.Split after Scan was called panics even when the first Scan returned false for empty input.
On an otherwise unused atomic.Value with no concurrent operations, Store accepts a typed nil pointer as a non-nil interface; Store(nil) panics, and the existing typed nil remains.
On an empty atomic.Value with no concurrent operations, CompareAndSwap("old", "new") returns false and leaves it empty; CompareAndSwap(nil, "new") initializes it and returns true.
